ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in an isosceles $\triangle ABC$ with $AB=AC=13$ and $BC=10$, $D$ is the midpoint of side $BC$, and $M$, $N$ are moving points on $AD$ and $AB$, respectively. What is the minimum value of $BM+MN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $BH\perp AC$ at H, intersecting AD at point $M'$, and draw $M'N'\perp AB$ at $N'$, then $BM'+M'N'$ is the minimum value sought.\\
Since $AB=AC$, and D is the midpoint on side BC,\\
thus AD is the bisector of $\angle BAC$,\\
therefore $M'H=M'N'$,\\
thus BH is the shortest distance from point B to line AC (perpendicular segment is the shortest),\\
since $AB=AC=13$, $BC=10$, and D is the midpoint on side BC,\\
thus $AD\perp BC$,\\
therefore $AD=12$,\\
since the area of $\triangle ABC=\frac{1}{2}AC\times BH=\frac{1}{2}BC\times AD$,\\
thus $13\times BH=10\times 12$,\\
solving yields: $BH=\boxed{\frac{120}{13}}$.

method.method_draft: Use a reflection/unfolding argument. From the image, read that A is at the left, B at the lower right, C at the top, D lies on BC, AD is drawn, M lies on AD, and N lies on AB with the broken path BM + MN shown. From the text, use AB = AC = 13, BC = 10, D is the midpoint of BC, M moves on AD, and N moves on AB. Since ABC is isosceles and D is the midpoint of BC, AD is the symmetry axis, so reflecting B across AD gives C. Therefore for any M on AD, BM = CM, and BM + MN = CM + MN. Thus the problem becomes finding the shortest path from C to line AB through some point M on AD and ending at N on AB. The shortest such path is the perpendicular distance from C to AB, and the perpendicular from C to AB intersects AD, giving feasible M and N. Compute AD = sqrt(13^2 - 5^2) = 12, area ABC = (1/2)(10)(12) = 60, so the altitude from C to AB is 2*60/13 = 120/13.

Then M=(t,0) for 0≤t≤12. For fixed M, the shortest possible MN with N on AB is the distance from M to line AB; check that the perpendicular foot lies on segment AB for 0≤t≤12. Since line AB through (0,0) and (12,-5) has equation 5x+12y=0, the distance from M=(t,0) to AB is 5t/13. Also BM=sqrt((12-t)^2+25). Thus minimize f(t)=sqrt((12-t)^2+25)+5t/13 on [0,12]. Differentiate: f'(t)=-(12-t)/sqrt((12-t)^2+25)+5/13. Setting f'(t)=0 gives 12-t=25/12. Substituting gives f_min=65/12+595/156=120/13.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in an isosceles $\triangle ABC$ with $AB=AC=13$ and $BC=10$, $D$ is the midpoint of side $BC$, and $M$, $N$ are moving points on $AD$ and $AB$, respectively. What is the minimum value of $BM+MN$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $BH\perp AC$ at H, intersecting AD at point $M'$, and draw $M'N'\perp AB$ at $N'$, then $BM'+M'N'$ is the minimum value sought.\\
Since $AB=AC$, and D is the midpoint on side BC,\\
thus AD is the bisector of $\angle BAC$,\\
therefore $M'H=M'N'$,\\
thus BH is the shortest distance from point B to line AC (perpendicular segment is the shortest),\\
since $AB=AC=13$, $BC=10$, and D is the midpoint on side BC,\\
thus $AD\perp BC$,\\
therefore $AD=12$,\\
since the area of $\triangle ABC=\frac{1}{2}AC\times BH=\frac{1}{2}BC\times AD$,\\
thus $13\times BH=10\times 12$,\\
solving yields: $BH=\boxed{\frac{120}{13}}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is above, forming triangle ABC; D is marked on side BC, segment AD has been drawn; point M is located on AD, point N is located on AB, and the broken-line path B-M-N has been drawn. Reasoning: From the problem statement, AB=AC=13, BC=10, and D is the midpoint of BC. Because triangle ABC is symmetric about AD, AD is the axis of symmetry, and the symmetric point of point B with respect to AD is C. For any M located on AD, BM=CM, therefore BM+MN=CM+MN. Thus the original problem is equivalent to: starting from C, passing through some point M on AD, then arriving at some point N on AB, making CM+MN shortest. The shortest case is the perpendicular segment from C to line AB; this perpendicular segment intersects AD, the intersection point can be taken as M, and the foot of the perpendicular as N, therefore it is feasible. Next calculate this altitude. Because D is the midpoint of BC, BD=5; in right triangle ABD, AD=sqrt(13^2-5^2)=sqrt(169-25)=12. The area of triangle ABC is (1/2)*BC*AD=(1/2)*10*12=60. When using AB as the base, the area also equals (1/2)*13*h, so h=2*60/13=120/13. Therefore the minimum value of BM+MN is 120/13.
